topic: Semaglutide and tirzepatide for obesity: weight-loss efficacy in clinical trials and main safety concerns

key_points.point: In the Wegovy label's 68-week obesity trial (STEP 1 per published literature; label calls it Study 2), semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -14.9% vs -2.4% placebo; 83.5% lost at least 5% and 47.9% at least 15%.

SURMOUNT-1 (2,539 adults without diabetes, 72 weeks): tirzepatide 5/10/15 mg gave about -15% / -20% / -21% mean weight change versus about -3% on placebo (label: -15.0/-19.5/-20.9 vs -3.1; efficacy estimand: -16.0/-21.4/-22.5 vs -2.4); roughly 85-96% lost at least 5%. Either set of figures counts.
Head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 (751 adults with obesity, no diabetes, 72 weeks): tirzepatide produced 20.2% mean weight loss versus 13.7% with semaglutide, with similar GI-dominated safety profiles.
Gastrointestinal events are the most common adverse reactions: with semaglutide 2.4 mg nausea 44% (placebo 16%), diarrhea 30%, vomiting 24%, constipation 24%; mostly during dose escalation.
Discontinuation due to adverse reactions with tirzepatide was about 5-7% across doses versus about 3% on placebo (label pooled: 4.8% / 6.3% / 6.7% vs 3.4%).

Both Wegovy and Zepbound carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors (seen in rodents; human relevance unknown) and are contraindicated with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

Beyond GI effects, label warnings include acute pancreatitis, acute gallbladder disease and acute kidney injury from volume depletion (also hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications in type 2 diabetes, severe GI adverse reactions and pulmonary aspiration under anesthesia); naming pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and one other warning counts.

Stopping treatment leads to substantial weight regain: in SURMOUNT-4, patients switched to placebo regained about 14% of body weight between weeks 36 and 88, while those continuing tirzepatide lost a further 5.5%.
EMA's PRAC concluded in June 2025 that non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) is a very rare side effect of semaglutide (up to 1 in 10,000 users); stop if confirmed.
Weight loss is smaller in people with type 2 diabetes: semaglutide 2.4 mg gave -9.6% vs -3.4% with placebo at 68 weeks (STEP 2; label Study 3).
Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, whereas semaglutide acts on the GLP-1 receptor only.

In the SELECT cardiovascular outcomes trial (label Study 1), semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90), and Wegovy carries this indication.
The FDA removed the suicidal behavior and ideation warning from the Wegovy and Zepbound labels in early 2026.
